A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nanostructured surfaces, by means of the "geometrical resonances" with proteins, can be considered as a powerful tool for the control of protein orientation and conformational state, with potential applications in tissue engineering and biotechnological devices.

nanostructured surfaces can be designed to orient proteins in a specific manner, thus allowing the control of the protein conformational state, the inter-molecular organization, and the related biological functions.
nanostructured surfaces with controlled curvature are able to induce a specific orientation of the adsorbed proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometrical matching of the adsorbent surface with the protein size and shape is a key factor in determining the protein conformation and orientation on nanostructured surfaces.
nanostructured surfaces with controlled nanoscale curvature are able to orient rigid proteins, such as laminin.

nanocurves can be used to orient proteins in a controlled way, thus allowing to modulate the protein configuration and to control the protein-protein interactions at surfaces, which can be of great interest for the development of new bio-inspired nanodevices for tissue engineering.
